issue: Hunter's prayer: woydéye causative 'show', 3du opt kʷḱih₁tā́m with dual h₃ókʷih₁, subj. dédeh₃oh₂ vow. Fine.

English 'Hear us, Father' has no PIE vocative in that sentence; active transitive perfect tetónth₂e 'you have stretched (yourself)' rendered 'you are stretched' (stretched sense). Relative-clause praise h₁yós … dʰéh₁s with 2sg verbs is good hymnic syntax.
Perfects dedr̥ḱmé, tetr̥pmé; neuter-plural subject with sg. h₁syéh₁t; mē + injunctive linékʷs. Fine.

Opening nékʷtbʰos is dat./abl. pl. where the address 'Night (and Dawn)' needs nom./voc. (kʷsép or nókʷts); méǵh₂ih₂ swésōr is singular against English 'great sisters' (dual swésorh₁e used at the end).
Healing prayer for a son: ḱéyor 'lies', aor. gʷʰért 'became warm (fevered)', optatives sth₂yéh₁t, mr̥yéh₁t, ph₃yéh₁t, Narten h₁édih₁t. Fine.

h₂yéwHō is the masculine nom. sg. of 'young' predicated of feminine h₂éwsōs; the feminine is h₂yuHénih₂ (used elsewhere in the batch). Also ǵn̥h₃tā́m 'did not recognise (each other)' for 'did not meet' is a stretched sense.
Night-voyage of the Sun: ḱémh₂t 'tired', accusative of goal dʰubʰróm wódr̥, instr. plówyoh₁, h₁íd for neuter sóh₂wl̥, woséyet bʰéh₂esh₁. Fine.
Spring hymn; aorist injunctive n̥ḱént for English present 'vanish' is the accepted convention; neuter predicate lewkóm priHóm agrees with neuter Sun addressee. Fine.
Question-and-answer hymn; common-gender kʷís for a female referent is normal; h₂óweyes 'sheep' kept apart from h₂éweyes 'birds'. Fine.
Tier 1 Lühr-type fable line: source notation (wlh₂néH, unmarked syllabic m in méǵHm, parenthesised (h₁é)); English omits gʷr̥Hḗi 'on a hill'.
méne h₃ókʷih₁ (nom. du.) ne dedwiyḗr: 3pl perfect with a dual subject. Engine gap: no PRF.3DU cell (as t023 66dc51f8). Use a present 3du, e.g. tréseti PRS.3DU, or drop the dual.
swéh₂i is loc. sg. fem. of the reflexive possessive; 'his own brother' needs acc. sg. masc. swóm agreeing with bʰréh₂term̥.
Tier 1 (Byrd, The King and the God) line; matches the source and the English.
Tier 1 laryngeal-less Schleicher-fable version (eḱwos, owei, wl̥nā, unaccented): notation clashes with corpus; English 'the sheep has' singular against plural owibʰyos.
War prayer to the Sun: ih₂dʰí, opt. unih₁mé, bʰugih₁ént, abl. n̥sméd, gʰostíbʰos with spr̥dʰí 'rescue from'. gʰóstis 'stranger' as 'enemy' follows Latin hostis; acceptable.
gʷnéh₂bʰos is dat. pl. 'to the women' for 'They gave the woman a gift' (one woman, as gʷnéh₂s later); needs dat. sg.
Shepherd's prayer: feminine anaphor h₁íh₂n̥s for sheep, wĺ̥kʷōd with h₂lékse, perfect optative lelikʷyéh₁t 'be left behind', vow dédeh₃oh₂. Fine.
dwóh₁ ḱwónh₁e (dual) h₁ím sékʷonto: 3pl middle imperfect with a dual subject. Engine gap: the deponent has no MID.PST.3DU cell. Use one dog (sékʷeto) or a plural.
bʰoydʰéh₂s is gen./abl. sg. as the object of dʰéh₁m̥ 'I made a pledge'; needs acc. bʰoydʰéh₂m (as 6d59d4c1) to agree with méǵh₂ih₂m.
Sky and Earth addressed as a pair: 2pl h₂élete and plural yúH pl̥th₂enṓs dʰubʰrṓs beside dual ǵénh₁torh₁e, ḱlutóm, ph₂stóm. Dual pronoun absent from closed class; the verb has PRS.2DU h₂életes.
Dawn-cattle myth (Vala type) is grammatical; lowkóm 'clearing, open space' rendered 'into the light' (stretched); swóns/h₁íns masculine for Dawn's cows follows the lexicon's m gender of gʷṓws.
Rain prayer: middle h₁áyso 'take' beside active h₁áydʰi 'give'; neuter-plural dʰewséh₂ with sg. tr̥syéti; loc. pl. h₂éǵroysu. Fine.
Solar hymn: neuter relative h₁yód agreeing with sóh₂wl̥, 2sg verbs throughout, closing imperatives. Fine.
Spring myth: fem. tgéwih₂ with fem. snígʷʰs, abl. wóyḱōd with linkʷént, gʷʰéros … h₁wésu neuter. Fine.
Prayer for a son: optative chain with h₁éy, vow déh₃oh₂. Fine.
Broken sun-wheel myth: twins with 3du gʷh₂tā́m, h₂réydʰetām, yugtā́m; masc. h₁éy for kʷékʷlos. Fine.
Dawn precedes Sun: 3du h₁r̥sḱétes for the pair, aor. sth₂mé. Fine.
ph₂ter n̥smé nékʷtbʰos h₂lékse is 'guard us from the nights' (abl. pl.); English 'in the night' (cf. kʷsépi).
